findings.title: Findings converge on the native side of the setSleepTimer contract (D4's interpretation function and the fixture case it is checked against)
findings.why_it_matters: Four findings land on one mechanism: what a fixture case contains and what D4's pure function receives and returns; patched one at a time the fixture shape gets decided four times.
findings.recommended: A: Re-evaluate the native side of the setSleepTimer contract before addressing Findings 2-5 individually
findings.chosen: A: Re-evaluate the native side of the setSleepTimer contract before addressing Findings 2-5 individually
findings.choice_reason: Re-evaluation settled: Android pins index encoding only; parse edge cases in with current outcomes; outcome out of contract, recorded as a limitation with no issue after code check showed the cross-file iOS case is re-armed at track change

findings.title: Android's chapter-timer meaning is resolved against live player state, not in the plugin method D4 extracts
findings.why_it_matters: A pure Android function over raw options pins only that the value is an integer; the meaning lives in the sleep-timer manager against live state.
findings.recommended: B: State in D4 and item 2 that Android's side of the contract is the index encoding

findings.title: The response half of the call (success) is not in the contract, and iOS reports success when it sets nothing
findings.why_it_matters: The motivating bug resolved success:true while doing nothing; the design pins only the argument half.
findings.recommended: B: Keep the contract to interpretation and file iOS's unconditional success as its own issue

findings.title: Absent, decimal and non-numeric time values already behave differently per platform, and Android crashes on some
findings.why_it_matters: Android's toLong() throws on a decimal and crashes the app via the bridge; iOS accepts it; a happy-path fixture hides this.
findings.recommended: A: Require item 2's fixture to include absent and decimal time cases

findings.title: A fixture case must tie the JS output to the native input, or the seam where the drift happened stays unchecked
findings.why_it_matters: Independent expectation columns let JS and native suites pass on different hand-written strings.

findings.title: D9's premise is wrong: the iOS job's build does not give XCTest what it needs, and a simulator failure meets a no-retry posture
findings.why_it_matters: The job builds for a generic simulator destination; tests need the test action on a concrete device, and a stuck simulator blocks merges with no retry.
findings.recommended: B: Correct D9, keep no retries, manual re-run, test-step timeout
findings.chosen: B: Correct D9, keep no retries, manual re-run, test-step timeout

findings.title: The iOS suite can only be built by pushing to CI, and a test left out of the target fails silently
findings.why_it_matters: objectVersion 48 needs hand edits for every Swift file; a test missing from the target passes silently.
findings.recommended: B: Rely on per-test job summary; PRs confirm their tests appear
findings.chosen: B: Rely on per-test job summary; PRs confirm their tests appear

findings.title: The ci-complete rollup and path filters don't cover the new jobs or the fixture as described
findings.why_it_matters: The rollup names jobs by hand; a new job left out doesn't block merges, and filters exclude design/** and *.md.
findings.recommended: A: Items 1 and 3 state rollup and filter edits; fixture outside excluded paths
findings.chosen: A: Items 1 and 3 state rollup and filter edits; fixture outside excluded paths

findings.title: A red iOS job can't be diagnosed from CI alone
findings.why_it_matters: -quiet output and no artifacts leave no view of which iOS test failed without a Mac.
findings.chosen: In Breakdown item 1: iOS tests as their own step without -quiet, executed tests and result in the job summary, result bundle uploaded on failure

findings.title: The parity check can pass while having extracted nothing
findings.why_it_matters: A parser broken by a refactor or cherry-pick extracts zero and the comparison passes.
findings.recommended: A: Print extraction, fail on zero per side, parser sample tests
findings.chosen: A: Print extraction, fail on zero per side, parser sample tests

findings.title: The Android JVM harness choice (plain JUnit or Robolectric) and a clock seam are undecided, and they shape item 4
findings.why_it_matters: android.* calls throw on the plain JVM; time-driven behaviors need a clock input.
findings.recommended: A: Plain JUnit; extracted logic takes current time as input
findings.chosen: A: Plain JUnit; extracted logic takes current time as input

findings.title: The JS bridge-arguments module needs the platform and chapter data as explicit inputs
findings.why_it_matters: Reading $platform and refs from the component needs the stub harness D1 avoided.
findings.chosen: In Breakdown item 2: the bridge-arguments module takes the platform and chapter data as explicit inputs

findings.title: Event payload fields are outside the parity check, and one already differs
findings.why_it_matters: Payload fields are unpinned; iOS's onSleepTimerSet omits isAuto (harmless today).
findings.recommended: B: Accept as a known limitation: the parity check compares event names, not payload fields
findings.chosen: B: Accept as a known limitation: the parity check compares event names, not payload fields

findings.title: The new JS job has to pick between the two Node versions already in CI
findings.why_it_matters: Android job uses Node 20, iOS Node 24; the JS job runs on one.
findings.recommended: B: Accept as a known limitation
findings.chosen: B: Accept as a known limitation

findings.title: time = "0" is overloaded on Android and the JS sends it for two different intents
findings.why_it_matters: Claimed stepping back to chapter 1 targets the current chapter; the guard at AudioPlayerContainer.vue:149-152 makes it unreachable.
